verses.13:2: Porque vós flagelais, e salvais: conduzis {inferos}, e {reducis}: * e não há quem escape da vossa mão.
verses.13:3: Dai graças ao Senhor, filhos de Israel, * e à vista das nações louvai-o:
verses.13:4: {ideo} entre as {ignorant}, * para que {narretis} as suas maravilhas,
verses.13:5: E lhes façais saber * que não há outro Deus {omnipotens} {praeter}.
verses.13:6: {ipse1} nos castigou por causa das nossas iniquidades: * e {ipse2} nos salvará por causa da sua misericórdia.
verses.13:7: Olhai, pois, o que ele fez conosco, e com temor e tremor dai-lhe graças: * e exaltai o Rei dos séculos {operibus}.
verses.13:8: Eu, porém, na terra do meu cativeiro lhe darei graças: * porque mostrou a sua majestade {ingentem} nação pecadora.
verses.13:9: Convertei-vos, portanto, pecadores, e {facite} diante de Deus, * crendo que ele {faciat}:
verses.13:10: Eu, porém, e a minha alma * nele nos alegraremos.
verses.13:11: Bendizei o Senhor, todos os seus escolhidos: * celebrai dias de alegria, e dai-lhe graças.

decisions.why: The canticle opens on the predicate, an acclamation, as the psalter's own Magnus Dóminus does (47:2, 95:4, 144:3, all 'Grande é o Senhor' in the finished psalms). Portuguese can front the adjective in an exclamation without strain; the pronoun is supplied because a bare 'Grande sois, Senhor' is clipped.

options.label: Grande sois vós
options.note: Draft. Keeps the Latin's first word first, as 47:2 / 95:4 / 144:3 'Grande é o Senhor'; ten syllables for the Latin's ten.

options.label: Vós sois grande
options.note: Plain order, as 85:10 'Porque vós sois grande' (magnus es tu, where the Latin itself has the pronoun after the verb). Loses the acclamation's lead.

options.label: Grande sois
options.note: The Latin word for word; eight syllables, and 'sois, Senhor' crowds the vocative.

decisions.latin: et in ómnia sǽcula regnum tuum
decisions.why: The colon has no verb in the Latin. DRB supplies 'is' (thy kingdom is unto all ages), MS1932 'existe'. In Portuguese the verbless colon still reads as a statement after 'Grande sois vós … para sempre', and the Latin's order puts the kingdom last, at the cadence, which a paroxytone 'reino' allows; the plain order would end on the proparoxytone 'séculos'. in ómnia sǽcula = 'por todos os séculos', as 144:13a regnum ómnium sæculórum → 'um reino de todos os séculos'; kept apart from bare in sǽcula → 'pelos séculos' (D43), since ómnia is the Latin's own word.

options.label: e por todos os séculos o vosso reino

forms.regnum: e por todos os séculos o vosso reino

options.note: Draft: verbless, as the Latin; ends on 'reino'.

options.label: e o vosso reino é por todos os séculos

forms.regnum: e o vosso reino é por todos os séculos

options.note: DRB's copula supplied; natural order, but the cadence falls on the proparoxytone 'séculos'.

options.label: e o vosso reino permanece por todos os séculos

forms.regnum: e o vosso reino permanece por todos os séculos

options.note: MS1932 supplies a full verb ('existe'); a verb the Latin does not have, and +3 syllables.

decisions.why: The psalter has the singular inférnus (19 verses), always 'inferno' in the finished psalms (open row: the blind readers hear the hell of the damned first). Here the Latin has the plural ínferi, the same phrase as the Canticle of Anna (DO Ps 223, 1 Sam 2:6 dedúcit ad ínferos et redúcit) and the Creed of DO Ps 234 (descéndit ad ínferos). The sense is death and return from it (God 'leads down … and brings back'), which the hell of the damned cannot carry. The Portuguese plural 'os infernos' is the traditional word for the realm of the dead, and keeps the Latin's number. dedúcere 'lead down' → 'conduzir', as 30:18 deducántur in inférnum → 'sejam conduzidos ao inferno' (the row's guiar is for guidance, D22). The ambiguity reader heard 'conduzis aos infernos' as 'you send to hell', and listed the plural 'infernos' as a word a listener may not know. Held for draft 2: the psalter renders inférnus 'inferno' throughout (an open row), 'trazeis de volta' in the same line tells the listener this is a place one comes back from, and changing the word here alone would split 212 from the rest of the psalter; the question is proposed as a glossary formula row (212, 223, 234) for a ruling, with 'à morada dos mortos' as the alternative.

options.label: aos infernos
options.note: Draft: the Latin's plural and word, the traditional Portuguese term for the realm of the dead. Not the living Creed wording — the Brazilian Apostles' Creed says 'desceu à mansão dos mortos' (circulation.md); the CNBB LH paraphrases this line as 'aos abismos da terra'. Proposed as a formula row for the three DO canticles that have ad ínferos (212, 223, 234).

options.label: ao inferno
options.note: The row's singular, as 30:18; drops the Latin's number and invites the hell of the damned, where God 'brings back'.

options.label: à morada dos mortos
options.note: Clear, and near the Brazilian Creed's 'mansão dos mortos' (verified, circulation.md); a paraphrase of one word (rule 2). MS1932 has 'até ao sepulcro', DRB 'to hell'.

decisions.why: redúcere → trazer is the open row (70:20 íterum reduxísti me → 'de novo me trouxestes', where íterum carried the return). Here there is no íterum, so bare 'trazeis' would lose the re-. MS1932 explains ('ressuscitas'); DRB 'bringest up again'.

options.label: trazeis de volta
options.note: Draft: the row's verb with 'de volta' for re-, as 70:20 took 'de novo'.

options.label: fazeis voltar
options.note: Shorter, but 'voltar' is convértere's verb in the glossary.

options.label: reconduzis
options.note: The cognate, echoing 'conduzis'; draft 1 of 70:20 had it and the stylist heard it as bureaucratic.

decisions.why: Quóniam → Porque (the default); ídeo 'for this reason' points forward to 'ut vos enarrétis' (ídeo … ut, 'to this end … that'). Word for word 'Porque por isso vos dispersou' stutters (the porque/por fault D14 names), and 'por isso' is heard in Portuguese as pointing back ('because of that'), which the ambiguity reader confirmed for draft 1's cleft 'foi por isso que'. 'para isto' points forward (isto, the near demonstrative, announces what follows) and is resolved by 'para que' in the second colon. The stylist found draft 1's cleft a pile of unstressed monosyllables and asked for a named subject so that 'vos' and 'o' do not blur: 'ele' is supplied (God, the subject since 13:3). dispérgere → dispersar: 43:12 'nos dispersastes entre as nações'.

options.label: Porque para isto ele vos dispersou

forms.ideo: Porque para isto ele vos dispersou

options.note: Draft 2: forward-pointing 'para isto', named subject (stylist); no cleft.

options.label: Porque por isso ele vos dispersou

forms.ideo: Porque por isso ele vos dispersou

options.note: The stylist's line: shorter, but 'Porque por' stutters and 'por isso' is heard as 'because of that'.

options.label: Porque foi por isso que vos dispersou

forms.ideo: Porque foi por isso que vos dispersou

options.note: Draft 1's cleft; heavy (stylist) and still heard as pointing back (ambiguity).

options.label: Pois para isso vos dispersou
options.note: Shortest; but 'pois' is kept for quia before questions (D42).

decisions.why: ignoráre is 'not to know'. The cognate 'ignorar alguém' is heard in Brazil first as 'to snub, to disregard someone' — a wrong sense. 34:15 et ignorávi → 'e eu não soube' already took the plain negated verb. 'não o conhecem' (DRB 'who know not him'; MS1932 'que o não conhecem') is the plain form; the cost is that 78:6 gentes quæ te non novérunt → 'as nações que não vos conhecem' has a different Latin verb, and here the two meet in one Portuguese. The Latinist asked for the comma the Latin has ('inter gentes, quæ ignórant eum'): the clause describes the Gentiles, all of whom do not know him; without the comma the Portuguese restricts it to some nations. Taken.

options.label: nações, que não o conhecem
options.note: Draft 2: the Latin's comma (Latinist).

options.label: nações que não o conhecem
options.note: Draft 1: restrictive.

options.label: nações, que o ignoram
options.note: The cognate; heard in Brazil as 'who snub him'.

decisions.why: The Latin names the subject, 'vos', where the verb alone would do: it is you, scattered, who are to tell. The stylist heard 'para que vós narreis' as a stiff s-n-r-r-s cluster and proposed the pronoun after the verb, where Portuguese puts an emphatic subject in a purpose clause. It keeps the Latin's word, and 'narreis vós' also marks the hearers (plural men) against the 'vós' of God (D1). Taken. 47:14 ut enarrétis (no vos) → 'para que narreis'.

options.label: narreis vós
options.note: Draft 2 (stylist).

options.label: vós narreis
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order.

options.label: narreis
options.note: As 47:14, where the Latin has no vos; drops the Latin's pronoun.

decisions.why: omnípotens is not in the 150 psalms (no row). 'todo-poderoso' is the plain Portuguese word and the Brazilian Creed's ('Creio em Deus, Pai todo-poderoso', verified, circulation.md); 'onipotente' is the learned cognate. MS1932 keeps 'omnipotente'.

options.label: todo-poderoso
options.note: Draft.

options.label: onipotente
options.note: The cognate (MS1932's, in the old spelling); one syllable shorter, more bookish.

decisions.why: 17:32 quis Deus præter Dóminum? → 'quem é Deus senão o Senhor?' fixes præter after a negation or question as 'senão'. MS1932 has 'senão ele' too; DRB 'besides him'.

options.label: senão ele
options.note: Draft, as 17:32.

options.label: além dele
options.note: 'besides him'; also good Portuguese, but departs from 17:32.

decisions.latin: Ipse castigávit nos … et ipse salvábit nos
decisions.why: The Latin names the subject twice where the verb alone would do: it is the same one who struck and who will save. 'Ele … e ele' keeps the repetition and the stress of a named subject; 'ele mesmo' (the ipse row, 94:5, 99:3a) says it more strongly but adds 3–4 syllables to cola already longer than the Latin. 98:6b et ipse exaudiébat → 'e ele os escutava' is the plain precedent.

options.label: Ele … ele
options.note: Draft.

options.label: Ele mesmo … ele mesmo
options.note: The ipse row's 'ele mesmo'; heavy at both heads.

options.label: Ele … ele mesmo
options.note: MS1932's build: the emphasis only on the turn to salvation; the Latin's two ipse are the same word.

decisions.why: in + ablative of means or sphere: exalt the King 'in' (by) your works. 'nas vossas obras' keeps the preposition, as 91:5 in opéribus mánuum tuárum → 'nas obras das vossas mãos'. MS1932 'com as vossas obras' makes the instrument explicit.

options.label: nas vossas obras
options.note: Draft.

options.label: com as vossas obras
options.note: MS1932; reads the in as instrument.

decisions.latin: osténdit majestátem suam in gentem peccatrícem
decisions.why: in + accusative: 'toward' (DRB) or 'upon / against'. The majesty was shown to a sinful nation — in the exile that punished it, or in the mercy that will save it; the verses around it say both (13:6). 'sobre' (MS1932) keeps both; the ambiguity reader heard it as 'over' (dominion), which is one of them. The Latin has no article. The Latinist proposed 'a nação pecadora' so as not to point away from Israel; refused: Latin gentem without a determiner is indefinite by default (DRB 'a sinful nation', MS1932 'uma nação pecadora', and 42:1 de gente non sancta → 'de uma nação'), and 'a nação pecadora' decides the other way, naming a nation already known. 'uma' leaves which nation open, as the ambiguity reader heard it ('some sinful people, without knowing which'). gens singular → 'nação' (42:1).

options.label: sobre uma
options.note: Draft: power displayed over; which nation left open.

options.label: sobre a
options.note: Latinist: the definite article, pointing to Israel (the 'nós' of 13:6).

options.label: a uma
options.note: 'mostrou … a uma nação pecadora': revelation to them.

options.label: para com uma
options.note: DRB 'toward'; leans to favour.

decisions.why: fácere justítiam → 'fazer a justiça' as 105:3 (et fáciunt justítiam → 'e fazem a justiça'); 'praticar' is kept for operári (14:2 operátur justítiam → 'pratica a justiça'). The article matters: bare 'fazei justiça' is heard in Brazil as 'take justice, avenge'. coram Deo → 'diante de Deus', as 55:13. MS1932 paraphrases ('sede justos'). The stylist heard 'fazer a justiça' as carrying out a sentence ('fazer justiça com as próprias mãos') and proposed 'praticai'; the ambiguity reader, on the same text, heard 'act justly / do what is right'. Refused: the article already keeps it from 'fazer justiça' (avenge), the listener heard it rightly, and 'praticar' is operári's verb, so taking it would merge two Latin verbs the psalter keeps apart (105:3 against 14:2).

options.label: fazei a justiça
options.note: Draft, as 105:3.

options.label: praticai a justiça
options.note: Stylist; clearer, but operári's verb (14:2).

decisions.latin: credéntes quod fáciat vobíscum misericórdiam suam
decisions.why: fácere misericórdiam cum aliquo has taken the idiom 'usar de misericórdia com' in 17:51 (fáciens misericórdiam Christo suo → 'usando de misericórdia com o seu Cristo'); 102:6 Fáciens misericórdias → 'faz misericórdias' kept the verb where there was no person. The Latin's subjunctive in reported belief is a future in Portuguese. vobíscum → 'convosco' (plural men; the vocative 'pecadores' in the first colon makes the addressee plain). The stylist heard 'usará convosco da' as breaking the set phrase 'usar de misericórdia' and proposed the complement first; taken — it is 17:51's order ('usando de misericórdia com o seu Cristo'), and the colon ends on 'convosco', the people addressed. The ambiguity reader listed 'usar de' as a word a listener may not know, but heard it rightly ('he will be merciful to you'); kept for 17:51.

options.label: usará da sua misericórdia convosco
options.note: Draft 2 (stylist): the set phrase kept whole, as 17:51.

options.label: usará convosco da sua misericórdia
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin's order (vobíscum before misericórdiam).

options.label: fará convosco a sua misericórdia
options.note: The Latin's verb, as 102:6; 'fazer misericórdia com' is a biblical calque.

choices.13:1: DO's Latin file opens with a heading line, '(Canticum Tobiæ * Tob. 13:1-11)', and DO's Portuguese file has its own heading ('(Cântico de Tobias * Tob. 13:1-11)'). It is DO's label, not a prayed verse and not a titulus of the book (the Clementine's 13:1 begins 'Aperiens autem Tobias senior os suum, benedixit Dominum, et dixit', which DO leaves out); render.py and checks.py skip it, as for the Nunc dimittis (233). Under D7 it is not translated here; if it is wanted for DO, 'Cântico de Tobias' is the plain rendering. DO's verse ids are its own: 13:1–13:11, where the Clementine numbers these lines 13:1–13:10 (DO splits Clementine 13:4 into 13:4 and 13:5) — DO's are kept. in ætérnum → 'para sempre' (D23). The Latin text is Jerome's Vulgate of Tobit, translated from an Aramaic text, not the Gallican psalter; the Greek (LXX 13:1–8) is a different text of the same prayer and not a witness of this Latin's sense. DRB and MS1932 (Tob 13:1b–10 in his numbering) translate this same Latin.
choices.13:2: Quóniam → Porque; 'vós' kept because the Latin has tu. flagelláre → flagelar (the flagéllum row, D39; 72:14 'fui flagelado'): kept apart from castigáre → castigar, which the canticle has four verses on (13:6); MS1932 'castigas' merges them. effúgere (not in the psalter) → 'escapar de', the Brazilian regency; MS1932 'subtrair-se à tua mão', DRB 'escape thy hand'. The first colon is 22 syllables for the Latin's 21.
choices.13:3: Confitémini Dómino → 'Dai graças ao Senhor' (D5). fílii Israël → 'filhos de Israel' (102:7, 148:14b), vocative without 'ó' (the Dóminus row's rule). in conspéctu géntium → 'à vista das nações', exactly 97:2. The Latin order is kept in the second colon (the nations before the verb, the verb last, a chiasm with the first colon); it is natural Portuguese, and it puts the nations where the next verse picks them up. The second colon is 3 syllables short of the Latin's 13 (checks) — accepted: nothing is dropped, Portuguese is simply terser here.
choices.13:4: enarráre → narrar (the open row; 47:14 ut enarrétis → 'para que narreis'); the Latin's own 'vos' is kept, after the verb (decision narretis). mirabília ejus → 'as suas maravilhas' (104:2, 95:3). gentes → 'nações' (twice in 13:3–4, as the Latin repeats géntium / gentes). The verse ends on a comma and runs on into 13:5, as the Latin does.
choices.13:5: faciátis scire eos → 'lhes façais saber' — 'fazer saber' is the Portuguese idiom for 'make know that'; scire here takes a 'that'-clause, which 'conhecer' (the open scire row) cannot, and notum fácere → 'fazer conhecer' is another Latin phrase. eos is masculine (the peoples, ad sensum); 'lhes' shows no gender. quia after scire is 'that' → 'que'. The first colon is 3 syllables short of the Latin's 9 — accepted: 'E façais que eles saibam' (−2) is heavier and adds a subjunctive the Latin does not have.
choices.13:6: castigáre → castigar (the working row castigáre / trádere, 117:18). propter → 'por causa de' (the row; 6:5 'por causa da vossa misericórdia'). iniquitátes nostras → 'as nossas iniquidades' (102:10). The two cola are built alike, as in the Latin.
choices.13:7: Aspícite → 'Olhai' (the aspícere row 'olhar para'; with a clause object Portuguese says 'olhai o que'). ergo → 'pois'. fecit nobíscum → 'fez conosco' (125:3 'fez conosco'); 'ele' supplied as subject after a string of imperatives addressed to the hearers. cum timóre et tremóre → 'com temor e tremor', the pair and its rhyme kept as in 2:11 (the working row). confitémini illi → 'dai-lhe graças' (D5, dative kept). Regem sæculórum → 'o Rei dos séculos': sæcula in the plural genitive, as 144:13a 'de todos os séculos'; not the D23 formula. exaltáre → exaltar (the row). Natural order in the second colon (the Latin fronts Regem with -que); the cola are 6 and 3 syllables short of the Latin's 28 and 18 (checks), accepted: every word is rendered, and 'confitémini' / 'Aspícite' shrink to 'dai graças' / 'Olhai'. The second colon's order also matches DO's antiphon for this canticle, 'Exaltáte Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris' (Psalmi major.txt 47, 325), so the antiphon can be cut from the verse. The stylist heard a hiatus in 'e exaltai' after the asterisk and proposed 'exaltai também'; refused: 'também' is not in the Latin (the -que is 'e'), and the two e-sounds of 'e exaltai' run together in speech and song without loss.
choices.13:8: Ego autem → 'Eu, porém,' (the row; 58:17, 74:10). captívitas → cativeiro (the row). majéstas → majestade (28:3, 71:19). osténdere → mostrar (4:6, 77:11). peccatrix → 'pecadora', the feminine of peccátor → pecador. confitébor illi → 'lhe darei graças' (D5). The first colon is 3 syllables short of the Latin's 20 (checks), accepted.
choices.13:9: Convertímini → 'Convertei-vos', as 89:3 (D25's exception: men told to turn to God, where 'voltai-vos' is also God's imperative in this psalter). ítaque → 'portanto', kept apart from ergo → 'pois' two verses before. peccatóres vocative, without 'ó'. credéntes → 'crendo' (the participle as a gerund, agreeing with the addressed sinners). In draft 2 the colon is 'crendo que ele usará da sua misericórdia convosco' (decision faciat).
choices.13:10: The Latin's plural verb with a double subject ('I and my soul … we shall rejoice') is kept: 'nos alegraremos'. lætári → alegrar-se (the row). 'nele' before the verb, as the Latin's 'in eo' before lætábimur, and it keeps the unstressed 'nos' from opening the colon after the pause (65:6 'ali nos alegraremos nele'). MS1932 recasts ('eu me regozijarei nele com toda a minha alma'); DRB keeps the double subject.
choices.13:11: Benedícite Dóminum (accusative) → 'Bendizei o Senhor', as 133:1a 'bendizei o Senhor, todos os servos do Senhor'. elécti → 'escolhidos' (the open eléctus row; 104:6, 104:43). ágite dies lætítiæ → 'celebrai dias de alegria' — the diem festum ágere row's verb, 'celebrar' (75:11); lætítia → alegria (104:43 'com alegria'). confitémini illi → 'dai-lhe graças', the same words as 13:7, as the Latin repeats them; the canticle ends as it has run, on thanksgiving (confitéri four times: 13:3, 7, 8, 11). The CNBB LH / Lectionary text has 'seus eleitos' here (circulation.md); 'escolhidos' is kept for the open eléctus row.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm212.txt (DO files the canticles as Psalms 210–273; this is the Tuesday Lauds canticle of the Roman psalter). Its first line is DO's heading '(Canticum Tobiæ * Tob. 13:1-11)', skipped by latin.py as every parenthesised line is. Compared with the Clementine Vulgate from bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-68-13.json, Tobiæ 13): the same words, the Clementine's intro clause of 13:1 omitted by DO, and DO's 13:4–13:5 = Clementine 13:4, so DO's 13:6–13:11 = Clementine 13:5–13:10. The printed Hetzenauer read was not done.

parallels.py 212 gives only the Latin and pt-PT for a canticle. Fetched: Clementine Vulgate and LXX Tobit 13 from bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-68-13.json, bolls-LXX-68-13.json — the LXX file is lemmatised, not the running text, and bolls has no DRB Tobit); DRB from drbo.org (consult/drbo-tobit13.htm → consult/drb-tobit13.txt); Matos Soares 1932 Tob 13 by pdftotext from the same PDF parallels.py uses (consult/ms1932-tobit13.txt; copyright, not committed). ps212/show.py prints the first three. The Vulgate of Tobit is Jerome's version from an Aramaic text and differs throughout from the Greek (LXX 13:2 εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς ὁ ζῶν where the Latin has Magnus es); so the Greek, used elsewhere as a test (D15), gives no evidence here, and the psalter's usage (concord.py) and DRB / MS1932 are the witnesses. No DM1962 text for this canticle. Precedents taken from the finished psalms by ps212/concord.py: 43:12 (dispersar entre as nações), 97:2 (à vista das nações), 17:32 (senão), 17:51 (usar de misericórdia com), 105:3 (fazer a justiça), 89:3 (Convertei-vos), 30:18 (conduzir ao inferno), 70:20 (trazer), 133:1a (bendizei o Senhor, todos…), 75:11 (celebrar), 2:11 (temor … tremor), 125:3 (fez conosco). Hardest: ad ínferos (the plural, and a formula shared with DO canticles 223 and 234), ídeo (a cleft), ignórant (a false friend in Brazil).

render.py and checks.py run with the DO number (212): hard checks pass (ids and pointing marks match the Latin; the heading line is skipped as for 233). Soft length flags on 13:3b (−3), 13:5a (−3), 13:7a (−6), 13:7b (−3), 13:8a (−3), each accepted in choices; no cadence flags. Circulation checked and recorded in ps212/circulation.md (CNBB LH Tb 13,2-8, Tuesday Lauds of week I, and the Lectionary's Tb 13 responsorial are the same Brazilian paraphrase of the Greek-based text; the Apostles' Creed wording). Shared tools: parallels.py gives only the Latin and pt-PT for a canticle (as for 233); worked around inside ps212/ with concord.py (the psalm number printed beside each hit), gloss.py, show.py and strip.py (HTML → text for circulation). No shared script was edited.
Draft 1. Two minor remarks: the comma of 13:4 taken; the article of 13:8 refused (kept as an option). Overall: faithful, marks right.

outcomes.reason: Latin gentem without a determiner is indefinite (DRB, MS1932, 42:1 'uma nação'); 'a' decides for Israel, 'uma' leaves it open.

audit.note: Draft 1. Five remarks: 13:4 cleft (taken in part: the cleft goes and 'ele' is named, but 'para isto' instead of its 'por isso'), 13:4 'narreis vós' taken, 13:9 order of 'usar de' taken, 13:9 'praticai' refused, 13:7 'também' refused. Worst line 13:4, best 13:6.

outcomes.remark: cleft 'foi por isso que' heavy; name the subject
outcomes.reason: Taken with 'para isto' rather than the proposed 'por isso', which stutters after 'Porque' and is heard as pointing back (ambiguity); the proposal stays as an option.
'praticar' is operári's verb (14:2) and 105:3 has 'fazem a justiça'; the article already keeps off 'avenge', and the ambiguity reader heard 'act justly'.

outcomes.remark: 'usará convosco da' → 'usará da sua misericórdia convosco'

outcomes.reason: 'também' is not in the Latin; 'e exaltai' elides naturally.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. Twenty items; most are the Latin's own openness heard rightly (Rei dos séculos, nas vossas obras, fez conosco, sobre, nele, dias de alegria). Acted on: 13:4 'por isso' heard as pointing back (fixed by 'para isto'). Held: 13:2 'infernos' heard as hell (psalter-wide row, flagged for ruling). Unknown words: flagelais, infernos, iniquidades, usar de — kept (glossary rows and 17:51).

audit.note: v2: 13:4 'Porque foi por isso que vos dispersou entre as nações que não o conhecem, * para que vós narreis' → 'Porque para isto ele vos dispersou entre as nações, que não o conhecem, * para que narreis vós'; 13:9 'usará convosco da sua misericórdia' → 'usará da sua misericórdia convosco'. Draft 1 is prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json, the file the v1 readers read).

Draft 2: hard pass. New soft flag 13:4a +3 (23 against the Latin's 20), accepted: the supplied 'ele' is the stylist's asked-for subject, and without it ('Porque para isto vos dispersou') 'vos' and 'o' blur again; the draft-1 flags (13:3b, 13:5a, 13:7a, 13:7b, 13:8a) are unchanged and stay accepted.

Draft 2. Clean: no remarks. It weighed and let stand 13:8 'sobre uma nação pecadora' (in + accusative open between 'toward' and 'upon') and 13:9 'usará da sua misericórdia convosco'. Marks confirmed (one mediant per verse).
